name: Question 5
problem: Find an equation of the plane that contains the point $Q(1,2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
worked_solution:
First, note that the position vector of $Q$ is $q=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ and $n=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point $Q({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n$ can be given as

$$
(r-q)\cdot n=0,
$$

where $r$ is the position vector of any point on the plane, and $q$ is the position vector of $Q.$

So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-q)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n-q\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =q\cdot n \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ r\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Find an equation of the plane that contains the point Q(1,2,−1) and is perpendicular to the vector n=[2−43].

a
r⋅[12−1]=−9
b
r⋅[12−1]=[24−3]
c
r⋅[2−43]=−9
d
r⋅[2−43]=[12−1]
e
r⋅[12−1]=−5
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, note that the position vector of Q is q=[12−1] and n=[2−43] is normal to the plane.

The equation of the plane that passes though the point Q(x0,y0,z0) and is perpendicular to the vector n can be given as (r−q)⋅n=0, where r is the position vector of any point on the plane, and q is the position vector of Q.

So, we have (r−q)⋅n=0r⋅n−q⋅n=0r⋅n=q⋅nr⋅[2−43]=[12−1]⋅[2−43]r⋅[2−43]=−9.
